label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Dear friends, neighbours, Little Acorns families, and everyone this reaches,

First, I’m safe. So is Marmalade. I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch, and I have somewhere to sleep, food to eat and people looking after me.

My phone hasn’t stopped since Saturday night. I’ve been crying at so many of your messages, and I’m grateful for every person who has checked in. I’m also very tired, and I can’t manage to tell the story or answer everyone individually right now. So I’m putting the important things in one place. Please feel free to forward this to anyone who’s been asking about me, or who wants to help.

For anyone who doesn’t know me, I’m Thandi. I teach the Ladybirds, the Grade 00 class at Little Acorns Pre-Primary in Mowbray, and I live in flat 12 at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory.

**What happened**

At around 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat in our block. My flat is on the second floor. Our neighbour, Uncle Faizel, went along our floor banging on every door, in his vest and slippers. That’s how I woke up.

I grabbed my phone and my cat, Marmalade, and got out. Nothing else came with me. Marmalade then hid under a car for two hours, which was a very long two hours, but she is safe.

Everyone in the block’s 14 flats got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and have since been sent home. The fire department has said it may have been an electrical fault, but they are still investigating. I don’t want to guess or pass on anything that hasn’t been confirmed.

My flat has extensive smoke and water damage, and the lounge ceiling came down. The landlord has said nobody can move back in for at least six weeks. There’s still a lot I don’t know about what can be saved and what happens next.

That’s as much of the story as I can tell for now. I’m not ready to go through all the details repeatedly, and I hope you’ll understand.

**What would help right now**

A few people have asked me to be specific, so here goes, even though asking feels very uncomfortable.

The things I need most are:

- **Help towards a deposit for a new place.** Having somewhere to live is the biggest thing I need to work out.
- **Shoes suitable for school/work, size 6, and work clothes, size 34.** I have enough everyday clothes now, but these particular things would help me get back into my school routine.
- **A working laptop.** If anyone has an older one they no longer use, I would be very grateful. It doesn’t need to be fancy. All my lesson planning was on mine, and I need something I can work on.

Please don’t feel you need to buy something new or give beyond what you can afford. If you have one of these things available, you can message me. I may take a while to reply, but I will get through the messages as I can.

**What I don’t need**

People have been incredibly generous with clothes already. I don’t need more general clothing at the moment, and I’ll pass the extras on to people from the other flats who can use them.

I also don’t need food right now. My sister’s freezer is full. Knowing that I’m fed and looked after is one less thing for anyone to worry about, so please save those offers for someone who still needs them.

**The fundraiser — and an important warning**

My friend Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy fundraiser for me:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**, and as of this morning it had reached **R11 400**. I’m honestly still struggling to take that in. Thank you to everyone who has donated or shared it.

I felt very strange about having a fundraiser. Zinhle’s advice was, essentially, “Shut up and accept it.” I’m trying to listen to her and accept the help people are offering.

Please be careful, though: there is also a page calling itself **“Thandi Fire Relief”**, as well as a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money to a **Capitec account**. **Those are not mine and are not connected to our fundraiser.** I have reported it.

The BackaBuddy link above is the only fundraiser I’m confirming. Please don’t send money to the other page or to the account in that WhatsApp message. If you’ve shared either of those, please send a correction to the same people. I’d really appreciate it if this warning stays attached when this letter is forwarded.

**To my Little Acorns parents**

The concert on **27 November is still happening**, and the Ladybirds will have crowns. Please don’t worry.

The 22 crowns I had brought home to laminate, along with the children’s handprint banner, were lost in the fire. That has been a particularly sore little part of all this. But we will sort out the crowns.

I’ll be back at school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of it in front of the children. I know any questions or hugs will come from kindness, but I’d really appreciate being able to settle into the day with them without talking through the fire.

**Thank you**

One of my children’s mums left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday. She didn’t even knock. Just quietly made sure I had something to wear. I keep thinking about that.

And about Uncle Faizel knocking on our doors. And my sister taking us in. And Zinhle doing the things I don’t have the energy to organise.

I’m upset about my home and my things. Of course I am. But furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t. I’m so thankful we got out.

Please don’t be offended if I don’t answer your DM, or if I’m slow to reply to comments. I’m not ignoring your kindness. I’m just taking things a little at a time.

Thank you for looking after me, and for understanding.

With love,  
Thandi
